{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Sparkling, the Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Software License and Maintenance Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly workable for us — the licence is perpetual while fees are paid, there is no auto-renewal, no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no liquidated damages and no audit right running against us, and we hold an unconditional 90-day exit right. The express warranty in § 12 is longer than our preferred position and is not undercut by any "AS IS" disclaimer.

The issues that require negotiation are concentrated in three areas. First, **liability**: § 15 contains no monetary cap at all, leaving our own direct-damages exposure unlimited, which fails both the preferred and fallback positions. Second, **assignment**: § 20(d) and § 3(c) impose a blanket bar on assignment by us with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out — walk-away territory — and the same restriction also narrows the licence grant under § 2. Third, **exit and risk allocation**: there is no transition assistance or data-return mechanic anywhere in the Agreement, and no vendor insurance requirement, notwithstanding that Garman installs on-premises and converts our data. We also need ownership language for Sparkling data and a licence back over the bespoke Modifications we pay for (§ 13), and a move off Nova Scotia law and venue (§ 20(h)).

Four findings are recorded as **needs review**: in each case the substantive position is at or above the playbook line, and the flag arises from a wording or keyword artefact rather than a drafting gap. We recommend confirming these on the record and not redlining them.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Needs review | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Vendor-to-Customer IP indemnity present and sits at the fallback; uncapped via the § 13/14 carve-out in § 15. Flag is a phrasing artefact (trigger drafted as breach of the ownership/non-infringement warranty). No redline. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns all IP in the Work including the bespoke Modifications we commission; our § 2 licence carries no modify/sublicense right, and no clause confirms we retain rights in our own data. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap of any kind; direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties, including us. Fails preferred and fallback on a material term. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); see also § 3(c)) | Blanket consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate or successor/M&A carve-out for us. **Walk-away territory.** |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity or sole-source obligation on us; grant is non-exclusive. Preferred position met. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, late interest or early-termination charge payable by us. Preferred position met. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Licence is perpetual and covers our affiliates, but is non-transferable (no successor transfer on M&A) and does not cover contractors or outsourced providers acting on our behalf. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; § 3 is limited to ordinary licence-scope protections. Preferred position met. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17(b) gives us an unconditional exit on 90 days' notice with no fee; no Vendor convenience right exists. Compliant at the fallback; flag is a labelling artefact. No redline. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No audit, inspection or verification right runs against us anywhere; the only examination right (§ 16 escrow) runs in our favour. At or better than preferred. No redline — raising it would invite one. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive Nova Scotia courts; Nova Scotia is not an accepted law, so the clause fails the fallback on both material terms. Not walk-away (home forum, non-exclusive, no arbitration). |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN or MFC obligation on us anywhere. Preferred position met. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap; fees payable per the Fee Schedule only. Preferred position met, subject to confirming Schedule "A". |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Drafted as a mutual **no-hire** reaching "any employee of the other party", with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Fails the fallback despite being mutual and 12 months. **Walk-away territory.** |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Needs review | § 10 Maintenance and Support | No auto-renewal; maintenance is a renewable one-year term by affirmative agreement. The 90-day figure is our own convenience right, not a non-renewal window. Preferred position met. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | Exit obligations run only on us; no transition assistance, data export or deletion certification anywhere. Fallback (90 days' assistance / 30-day export) also unmet. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Conformance warranty through acceptance, a full year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and while Maintenance continues, with a repair remedy and refund on rejection; no "AS IS" disclaimer. At or above preferred. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 10 (§ 20 General Matters) | No insurance or certificate requirement anywhere, notwithstanding on-premises installation and data conversion. **Walk-away territory** per the rule. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These three items are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **Assignment (§ 20(d), § 3(c))** — the blanket prohibition on assignment by us, with no affiliate or successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, is a blocker. We need the affiliate/successor carve-out, consent not unreasonably withheld, a no-assignment-to-a-competitor limit on Garman, and § 3(c) conformed.
2. **Non-solicitation (§ 19)** — a mutual no-hire covering all of the other party's employees, with no carve-outs, is a blocker. We need it converted to a narrow 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and the no-hire deleted.
3. **Vendor insurance (absent)** — the complete absence of any insurance covenant, where Garman installs on-premises and converts our data, is a blocker. We are inserting the model coverage as a new § 20(j), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback available.

We would also treat the **uncapped liability position in § 15** as close to a condition: as drafted, our own direct-damages exposure is unlimited.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on the seven items with proposals: § 15 mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims and fees excluded from the cap); § 20(d)/§ 3(c) assignment carve-out; § 19 non-solicit narrowing; new § 20(j) insurance; new § 17(d) transition assistance, 30-day machine-readable data return and certified deletion; § 13 Sparkling data ownership plus perpetual licence back over the bespoke Modifications; § 2 contractor use and successor transfer; § 20(h) New York law and exclusive New York County venue.
2. **Set the negotiation order** — lead with assignment, non-solicitation, insurance and the liability cap; treat governing law as tradeable (Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London remain acceptable fallbacks).
3. **Do not redline the four needs-review items** (indemnity, termination for convenience, audit, renewal). We recommend confirming the substantive position internally and, where useful, in correspondence rather than in the document — in particular, we should not raise the absence of an audit right, since doing so invites Garman to introduce a verification obligation we do not currently owe.
4. **Obtain and review Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule)** to confirm it carries no committed user or location counts and no minimum annual maintenance spend, and Schedule "D" to confirm the scope of the Modifications covered by the § 13 licence back.
5. **Raise commercially, not by redline** — a CPI/3% cap on renewal-period maintenance uplift and a 60-day renewal reminder, to be handled in the Fee Schedule negotiation; and, if pricing benchmarking matters to the business, an MFN running in our favour.
6. **Diligence the operational points behind the indemnity** — the ten-calendar-day notice obligation on us under § 13 should be diaried into our claims-handling process, given there is no express defence-and-cooperation mechanic."}
